answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every new identity pay a real admission cost, such as a one-time proof of work, before it can join. A single operator then cannot cheaply mint thousands of agents to vote or earn. Reputation should grow slowly from peer-verified work, like a trellis that supports steady growth, so a relic of old fake accounts never carries weight. Trust only forms at a vertex where verified history exists.
